title: Unplug a palm router, then hold its spindle lock while the other hand frees the bit
instruction: Take the bit out of the router and stand it in the bit block.
context: Changing a router bit is one of the commonest woodshop jobs, and the manual for the Bosch PR20EVS Colt palm router (about $130) carries Bosch's rule: "Disconnect the plug from the power source and/or the battery pack from the power tool before making any adjustments, changing accessories, or storing power tools." A router that starts with a wrench on its collet nut throws the wrench and spins the bit under the fingers, so the plug must be out before the wrench or a hand goes near the bit. The Colt's one-wrench change then needs both hands at once: one presses the spindle lock in and keeps it in, because the spindle turns freely on its bearings, while the other turns the 17 mm collet nut loose with the supplied wrench. Let the lock go and the wrench just turns spindle, nut and bit together. This is the bit change itself, start to finish, not routing.
setup:
Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the work board's top. Work board: a 19 mm plywood board over the table with a 76 mm hole for the router, on 100 mm risers; the arm bases sit on spacer plates of the same 119 mm, so all heights match the simulation and nothing is cut into the station. Figures marked est are design values; real parts are matched by the checks in brackets.
Router: a Bosch PR20EVS Colt motor (75 mm across, blue), out of its base, stands collet up in a 76 mm hole in the work board, its lower half below, held fixed (it cannot turn, tip or lift) by a padded split clamp collar bolted under the board round its body, its spindle axis at (230, 0); the housing's top shoulder is 90 high, the 1/4 in collet nut (17 across flats, 15 tall) runs from 100 to 115. The spindle-lock button (black cap 14 x 12, proud of the housing by 7) faces the robot at 75 high, pressed along +x; its pin enters one of six notches in the spindle's lock disc after 3.5 of its 5 travel, against a 6 N spring at the stop (est; push it in with a spring scale). With the lock out the spindle turns freely (est 0.002 N m s). The collet nut is reset to 0.5 N m before every trial with a torque screwdriver and a 17 mm socket (0.3 to 1.2 N m range), and the simulation's nut breaks free at the same 0.5 N m. The nut starts with a pair of flats parallel to a heading 7 deg left of +x (its mark lined up with one on the board); the lock pin then faces a notch (est). The collet lets go of the shank once the nut is 40 deg loose (est; marks on the nut and on the spindle shaft, turn until the bit lifts out by hand).
Bit: a protected stand-in, a 1/2 in straight bit on a 1/4 in shank with its cutting edges ground off and the cutter painted brass: shank 20 long (14 in the collet), cutter 12.7 across and 20 long, top at 141, 30 g.
Wrench: the 17 mm collet wrench supplied with the router, open jaw (17.3 gap), 152 long, 18 wide, 4 thick, 55 g (est), lying flat on a wooden rest block (104 x 34 x 25) with its jaw at (180, 260) pointing to -x and its handle overhanging the block's +x end by 50.
Power strip (never connected to mains in real trials: its own cord is cut off and its lit switch is a painted mark, so the router cannot be energized; the plug-in state is shown only by the plug's position): a white 6-outlet strip standing on its back edge, outlets facing the robot, face at x 180, from y -290 to -90, 45 tall, switch on. The router's plug (black, 22 x 25 x 30) is in the outlet at y -150, held at 3 N (est; pull it with a spring scale); its blades are 16 long. The cord runs on the bench from the plug round to the router's front.
Bit block: a wooden block 60 x 30 x 20 centred at (230, 335) with three 10 mm holes along x, 18 apart.
Start: both arms at the ready pose, grippers open; the router plugged in.
scoring:
Read every control step from the plug's travel, the nut's turn on the spindle, the bit's and the wrench's poses and the grippers' finger zones; the score is the last step's.
Live: the plug drawn out less than 16 mm (its blades still in the contacts).
Scored 0 for the rest of the trial, at any moment: while live, the wrench's jaw on the nut (its centre within 15 mm of the spindle axis at nut height), or any finger within 10 mm of the bit; the bit or the wrench off the bench.
Otherwise:
0 = still live (the untouched start, or plugged back in).
0.25 = unplugged.
0.5 = unplugged and the nut turned 0.7 rad (40 deg) or more loose on the spindle.
0.75 = the bit out of the collet (its shank's end 2 mm or more above the nut's top, or off the axis), not yet done.
1.0 = on every step of the last 1 s: the bit standing shank-down in a block hole (shank end within 3 mm of a hole's centre and 10 mm or more below the block's top, tilt under 15 deg), the wrench lying flat on the bench or its rest block with its jaw 50 mm or more from the spindle axis, both grippers' finger zones 50 mm or more from the bit, and the bit and the wrench each moving under 5 mm.
Real trial: check the plug's travel with a ruler on video; the nut's turn is read from the top camera between a white line on the nut's top face and a white line on the bit's cutter top (the bit turns with the spindle until the collet lets go, so the housing is not the reference); the rest from the video.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The lock is contact only (a sprung pin into notches); the nut's grip is joint friction at the 0.5 N m the real nut is reset to; the collet's release is a glue joint let go at 40 deg; the plug is a slider held by 3 N of friction; the motor's lower half is hidden in the well. Estimates (est) are listed in the setup with how each is checked. The bit is a blunted stand-in.
reset_notes: Unplug if needed. Put the bit's shank back in the collet 14 mm deep, tighten the nut to 0.5 N m with the torque screwdriver while holding the lock in, release the lock, turn the spindle until the nut's mark lines up with the board's, lay the wrench flat on its rest block with its jaw at the mark, push the plug fully into its outlet, and park both arms.
